prompts.men_cham: Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept. Title/concept: MEN CHÀM — A LIVING CERAMIC WORLD. An audacious sophisticated game art direction where the whole world appears shaped from BLUE-AND-WHITE GLAZED CLAY: warm milky-ivory porcelain planes, deep hand-painted COBALT BLUE brushwork, tiny controlled grey crackle used as material accent, very small raw terracotta exposed edges. This is NOT a scene of a normal village containing ceramic pots: people, bamboo houses, leaves, soil terraces and river ALL share ceramic forms and cobalt motifs. Mature expressive people have intentionally sculpted angular adult proportions and distinct strong faces; faces shaped as smooth ivory clay with a few decisive cobalt marks for eyes/brows/wrinkles, not doll faces, not chibi porcelain toys, not fragile broken bodies. Clothing is modeled as broad folded ivory planes with asymmetrical cobalt stripes rather than ornate floral chinoiserie. Individual young adult and older potter have distinct silhouettes. World scene: elevated three-quarter view through a small village pottery market courtyard beside a narrow stream, broad quiet path, one craftsperson showing a repaired water jar to an arriving protagonist, neighbors trading baskets nearby. Stylized ceramic leaves cluster into clean simple blue/white masses; water is pale smooth enamel with a few deep cobalt ripples. Glaze reflects only very restrained soft daylight, no blown shiny plastic highlights, no gold trim or generic Chinese dragon pattern. UI: asymmetrical ceramic plaque shapes and clean tile-like inventory recesses, ivory fields with crisp COBALT ink typography, selected outline as thick cobalt brush-stroke plus tiny terracotta notch; dialogue portrait feels like the same modeled/painted clay face, item icons are economical cobalt silhouettes with limited clay shading. Text fields mostly MATTE IVORY, no crackle or glare behind words. The journal has a sparse cobalt sketch and dark blue type. Strong calm value grouping and open spaces, not uniform crackle noise. Design an original, elegant world-wide material metaphor suitable for living-world RPG art, not a souvenir showroom or tabletop island. One wide 16:9 WHOLE-GAME VISUAL DIRECTION BOARD. Top roughly two thirds: a believable complete game-screen mockup with actual designed HUD/navigation, a dialogue portrait and choices, and an inventory panel. Bottom roughly one third: three clean adjoining sample panels showing TWO full-body adult character designs, THREE distinct expressive portrait closeups, and enlarged item/inventory/journal UI specimens. Include all requested regions fully within image, no oversized title area. Exact short Vietnamese navigation: 'Thế giới', 'Cuộc đời', 'Túi đồ', 'Nhật ký'. Dialogue choices: 'Hỏi chuyện', 'Giúp việc', 'Rời đi'. Six simple noncombat item icons: rope coil, clay water jar, herb bundle, woven basket, grain sack, wood adze. UI text quiet, high contrast, generously spaced, sparse and readable; no ornamental marks instead of letters. Selection uses an outline/notch plus color, not color alone. Inventory/journal closeup has real slots, icons, one selected state and one short entry. Whole board must use one coherent style across WORLD, BODY SHAPES, FACES, PORTRAITS, ITEM ICONS AND UI, not a stylized scene under generic modern buttons. Plain Vietnamese-inspired bamboo/thatch/stilt structures, ordinary villagers, professions/family/social interaction. This is fictional graphic inspiration, not archaeology or a claim about an ancient art tradition. No character customization/origin choices, no weapon action bar, no combat spectacle, no torii, pagoda roofs or Chinese lantern streets. The board is entirely an IMAGE CONCEPT, not actual gameplay, animation, 3D model or engine output. No watermark, no A/B/C version letters, no irrelevant English labels. The two fullbody samples must be the protagonist and artisan/elder who also appear in main scene, portraits in the same drawing/material grammar.
prompts.bong_roi: Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept. Title/concept: BÓNG RỐI — A GAME AS A LIVING BACKLIT SHADOW STAGE. An audacious cohesive graphic game world made of thin articulated cut silhouettes and perforated translucent shapes, seen as colored light/shadow on layered illuminated screen planes. MAIN WORLD and CHARACTERS are strong near-black or warm charcoal silhouettes with selected amber, parchment and faded cinnabar translucent inserts, tiny cut perforations indicating woven clothing or wrinkles. No photorealistic skin, no painterly landscape, no 3D miniature dolls. Adult humans have individual readable noses/jaws/hair profiles and expressive hand gestures, mature dignified body proportions; joints subtly visible as an artistic rule, not mechanical robot limbs. Distinct elderly village woman and young working protagonist, not interchangeable shadow monsters. Faces in portrait closeups use the same cut/profile/perforated grammar and enough warm light to read emotion. Scene: lateral-oblique walkable bamboo bridge over a swollen river at dusk, adult protagonist in conversation with an older villager carrying a grain basket, a family moving bundled belongings along a raised path; modest stilt-house and reed layers recede behind. Large warm PARCHMENT-LIGHT negative spaces between black reed and roof silhouettes, few vermilion translucent cloth accents. Layered backlight gives only thin local shadows, NO blurry cinematic orange/teal grading or all-over darkness. UI is also a backlit crafted screen: pale luminous parchment windows within irregular ink-black cut frames, readable deep charcoal Vietnamese type; tabs are simple cut shapes, inventory icons are clean perforated silhouettes in pale lit slots, selected state a notched vermilion rim with a white aperture; journal diagrams share cut-shadow marks. Text blocks use bright calm untextured parchment, not lace patterns. No external theater audience, proscenium stage border, visible giant puppeteer's hands or control rods covering the playing field: the image should feel like an entire navigable WORLD expressed through shadow theater, not a photograph of a puppet performance.
